title: AS IN THE DAYS OF NOAH: PAST & PRESENT

sense.text: “One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh”: the old die and the young are born, one generation after another. Generations have a cycle, a circuit, the same as everything else Solomon names after it. Hold on to that, because the whole passage comes back to verse 4.
“The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.” Like the generations, the sun has a cycle: it rises, it goes down, and it comes right back around.

The wind turns about from the south to the north, “and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.” The wind has circuits, cycles, just as generations have circuits and cycles. The moon has its cycles too.

“All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full”, and “unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.” The rivers flow into the ocean and the ocean flows back into the rivers. It is a cycle.
“The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.” We can hear of it and we can see it, but it is so wondrous that we cannot behold all of it.

Now Solomon turns from the sun, the wind and the rivers to something else: “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. Keep the context: generations, the sun, the wind, the rivers, all going around. So “there is no new thing under the sun.”

“Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.” The thing that hath been is the thing that was before, before our generation, in the past. And the thing is man (Ecclesiastes 6:10). Man has been here before. Just as the sun goes up and down and the rivers flow into the ocean and back again, we come and we go. You and I have been here before, in different cycles of life. That is why verse 4 begins with one generation going and another coming.

That is why there is déjà vu, a French term that means already seen. You are living out what you were predestined to see in the first place; your mind is catching up to a moment that was already ordained to take place. The prophets saw things in their visions and they came to pass. When the prophets saw us going on slave ships, we had to live it out. When John saw America in flames, we have to live out what John already saw. We are catching up to the prophecies, and what leads up to what John saw is already set in motion. You cannot change what has already been seen.
“There is no remembrance of former things”. Man has been around before, but there is no remembrance of us being around before. That is what Solomon is talking about.

precepts.why:
More clues to what the thing is: “That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been”. That thing which is to be has already been.

“And God requireth that which is past.” God requires that thing which was in the past.

Solomon gave a hint, and here he explains it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. The thing that hath been is man. Man has been already.

“Neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” So what Solomon is telling us in chapter 1 is that the thing that hath been, which shall be again, is man.

“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?” The wise man knows the interpretation of the thing, and the thing that hath been is man.

Man has been around before, but there is no remembrance of us being around before. Like the wind, the sun, the moon and the rivers, man comes and goes: we have always been here, in different cycles of life.

The Lord says, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is round, like time on a clock, going around and around. So life, man and the judgments of God come around over and over. That is why Solomon said there is no new thing under the sun: no man is new, we have all been here before. People say, he reminds me of so-and-so, grandpa used to do that. That might be grandpa, or great-grandpa, come around again.

Like the rivers, the wind, man and the sun, judgments also have a circuit, a cycle in which they happen over and over again. America is a compilation of every captivity we have been in, from Egypt all the way to Rome, even Spain and Portugal. That is why America is the worst and the last: it is an amalgamation of every captivity we have served from the beginning of our time as a nation.

America took all those ancient civilizations and merged them into itself to strengthen itself. America is young, 250 years old this year, while Persia goes back thousands of years and Britain hundreds. But America acquired a lot of power in very little time because it learned from the mistakes of all the ancient fallen civilizations before it.

sense.text:
“The Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”: God formed Adam from the soil of the earth, meaning he was a brown or dark man. The richer the soil, the darker the soil, so Adam was a very, extremely dark man.

Not a single scientist will tell you that Adam and Eve were two Caucasian people that gave birth to Negroes. It is impossible for recessive, degenerate genetics to produce the different hues of brown. Adam and Eve were the darkest, and gave birth to every spectrum of color known to mankind. The original man and woman were black, and the white man cannot argue it.

The white man is new compared to the black civilizations way before his time: Egypt, Babylon, every ancient civilization was black people. We are new as well in a way, because Jacob came out moments after Esau was born, and we were the last nation on earth. But in terms of color, Esau is brand new, because everybody was dark.
The Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, took one of his ribs, and of the rib “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.”
“She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Woman means out of man, of man.
“They shall be one flesh.” This is the first time we read of the institution of marriage: Adam and Eve.

Satan went to Eve, tempted her and seduced her into partaking in idolatry, and Adam and Eve were chastised for it: “the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.”

“So he drove out the man”: Adam got evicted. Adam and Eve were kicked out of the garden, out of paradise.

“He placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.” The cherubims are angels. To keep the way means to keep you away from it, so that you cannot enter again: angels set there to cause confusion so you cannot go back. And mark where they were placed: “at the east of the garden of Eden.”

“Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain”. Cain is the firstborn they had once they were cast out of the garden.

Eve said, “I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Keep that in mind: Cain was a man from the Lord.
“Abel was a keeper of sheep”: Abel was a shepherd. “But Cain was a tiller of the ground”: Cain spent most of his time in the field. And Jacob was a shepherd.

“In process of time”: it does not say how long, years or months, but it took place gradually, over time. Nothing new under the sun.

“Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord”, because Cain spent his time in the field.

Abel, being a shepherd, “brought of the firstlings of his flock”: the firstlings are the best of his flock. “And of the fat thereof”: once Adam and Eve were cast out they had to sacrifice animals from that point on. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering”.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” The Lord said, what the hell is that? You got me some apples and oranges and bananas? He had no respect for Cain’s offering at all.

“And Cain was very wroth”: Cain was pissed off. “And his countenance fell”: his face changed real quick.

“Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” What are you upset about?

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you do what I told you to do, which is offer up an animal, will I not accept it? You brought me fruit; I asked you for the firstlings, like your brother brought. In process of time Cain got sick and tired of bringing animals and began to gain a certain level of resentment for offering to the Lord.

“And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Sin is the devil, Satan, and the door is not an actual door; it is in your mind. If you do not do well, Satan will take control of you.

“And unto thee shall be his desire”: you will want to do what Satan wants you to do. “And thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over you and use you as a vessel.

“And Cain talked with Abel his brother”: all right, Lord, no problem. Hey Abel, let me talk to you for a second. “When they were in the field”, where Cain spends his time, “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

“Where is Abel thy brother?” The Lord knew exactly what happened, and tested Cain to see where his mind was and whether he had a conscience.

“I know not”: that alone is disrespectful, and the hatred he had when he killed his brother was still there. “Am I my brother’s keeper?” Am I his babysitter? Now he is talking smart to the Lord.

“The voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.” Your brother is right here with me. You killed your brother.

“And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand”. The blood he spilled that hit the ground is placed upon him by cursing him from the ground. And what was Adam made of? The dust of the ground. Curse that ground, and that ground is not the same color. Something happens to that color. That same blood he spilled, he is going to match it.

“When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength”. Remember he was a man of the field. Bring it to today: when the so-called white man needs resources, does he stay in Europe? Europe has grain and resources, but not in the abundance of Africa. If it were not for Africa, Europe would be a third world country. That is why the white man had to go to the Americas and to Africa, where Israel is, to acquire resources. The white man is a scavenger.

“A fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.” A vagabond is a bum: you will wander around, in this land and that land, where you do not belong. Bums sleep where they do not belong: the subway, the sidewalk, the bus station, the staircase, the elevator, under the bridge. They are found where they should not be. A fugitive is one who escapes from the law for his crimes and has not served his sentence yet. That is the lot of Cain and his seed after him.

“My punishment is greater than I can bear.” “Thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God will deal with him no more. Who will deal with him now? Satan. Remember God told him, “unto thee shall be his desire.” God is not his God any more, and that curse fell upon him and his children.

“Every one that findeth me shall slay me.” How would anybody know he was that murderer? He would look different. That melanin is gone. Examine the so-called white man today: you see his blood flowing right through his skin. He is red, like the same blood that Cain shed in that ground.

“Whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.” No one is to touch him or avenge Abel’s blood; he is a fugitive, and the Lord does not want him to serve for his crimes yet. He will deal with him himself.

“And the Lord set a mark upon Cain”: that is the curse in the ground.

“Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.” On the east of Eden is the same place where the cherubims and the flaming sword were, that cause the confusion. That is where Cain went, and who do you think he dealt with over there? The devil.

“Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch”, his firstborn son. “And he builded a city”, and a city has a population. There was a whole bunch of people around at this time, not just Adam and Eve and Cain. Adam and Eve had children, and that is where Cain got his wife.

He “called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” Cain built a city, and that city was called Enoch.

“Cush begat Nimrod”: Cush, one of the four sons of Ham, begat Nimrod. These are Hamites. “He began to be a mighty one in the earth”: he became powerful, an elite leader that people followed. Mighty, and evil as hell also.
“He was a mighty hunter before the Lord”: he hunted after men, a man of the field too. When it says mighty hunter, it means he was a very evil leader and ruler.

“The beginning of his kingdom was Babel”, which is Babylon, “and Erech”, which is Uruk, Iraq today, “and Accad”, the Akkadians, that area of Mesopotamia and Sumer, “in the land of Shinar”, which is Sumer and the vaster area in which Sumer is found.

The white man does not want to know this, so he hides this history, because if you prove Nimrod existed, the Bible is given validation. So they say the first king of Babylon was Sargon of Akkad, which means king of Akkad, one of the first rulers of Babylonia. That is Nimrod, and when he died they deified him as a god.

Cain named his city after his son Enoch. The Sumerians called the city Unug or Unuk, as in Enoch; the Akkadians called it Uruk, which is Iraq. Older Assyriologists, the scholars who studied Assyria, identified Cain’s city of Enoch with Unug, in the region later called Babylonia, and held that the Babylonian civilization was built on, and inherited, the civilization that began with Cain. So Nimrod built on top of the ruins of Cain’s city. Today its ruins are called Warka, southeast of Baghdad, not far from where Abraham was from.

Modern scholarship, much of it secular or atheist, comes behind those older scholars and says they were wrong, to remove any validation of the Bible out of history. That is why the best books are the oldest ones, closer to that time. But it is true: Cain did build in that area, and Nimrod built on top of it. That is where the evil was, and that is why the Lord told Abraham to leave there.
Peter says, “Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?”

“In the regeneration”: our spirit has been here before. “When the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory”: the Son of man is not sitting on his throne right now, in the kingdom of heaven on earth. The regeneration is when he comes back and is on his throne on the earth.

“Ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” That proves the disciples are not sitting on the thrones right now, and are not judging the twelve tribes of Israel yet.

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over you, and you shall acquire your power from Satan.

Read the commentaries on this verse and they tap dance around it and do not want to be honest about it. Be very careful of modern scholarship, because they hide things; the older scholars are more upfront. There is a movement set up to censor and hide any biblical truth that can be substantiated, to give the Bible no validation.
“Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”: he killed his brother.

“I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?” He is lying. What is Cain showing? No accountability. He kills, and says, I am not his keeper.

That is what Esau does today. We were all on the boat, we don’t know what happened to him; here’s his phone, here’s his keys; let’s get a lawyer, call your mom, she’s a judge. I walked into the house and he was in my house, I shot him, but it was his apartment: I don’t know what happened. The sister in Tanzania: she hung herself, and he left the country, and the charges were dropped. No accountability.

We didn’t enslave you; you enslaved each other. It wasn’t a slave trade, it was a slave migration. What ships? What Middle Passage? What is the Clotilda? You speak an African language in South Carolina, Geechee? No accountability. Not guilty. It is the same thing.

And black folks adopt the same thing: get over it, that was thousands of years ago. We were emancipated in 1865, 161 years ago. Civil rights came in 1965, 61 years ago, and that is not old. Sharecropping was slavery, and it secretly lasted until 1960. We held up signs saying I am a man, because after the Emancipation Proclamation we were being treated like slaves, killed and hung: the KKK, Jim Crow, Juan Crow, criminal leasing laws, vagrancy laws, black codes, burning our cities down, flooding our cities, bombing our cities. They changed the Tulsa massacre into the Tulsa riot. What riot? They flew planes over us and dropped dynamite on top of us. No accountability.

Matt Walsh, no accountability. Charlie Kirk said all the violence in the earth is done by black people, and he got killed by a white man. Look how God cook.

precepts.why:
Christ, speaking to his own people, the same Jews who were plotting to kill him: “Ye are of your father the devil”. Remember the Lord said to Cain, from thy face shall I be hid. Who became Cain’s father? The devil.

“And the lusts of your father ye will do”: the same way Cain killed his brother, you are going to kill me. The same spirit that was in Cain is in you.

“He was a murderer from the beginning”. Did Satan murder anybody? No. Satan introduced death, but he did not kill anyone. Who killed in the beginning? Cain. The commentaries and the modern consensus say this is Satan. It is not; it is talking about Cain.

“And abode not in the truth”. Remember, in process of time Cain offered up fruit when he was supposed to offer up animals. He abode not in the truth. It cannot be talking about Satan: Satan was always a liar, that is his job; devil means liar, the opposite of the truth.

“When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.” When the Lord asked Cain where his brother was, he said, I know not. He was lying.

Remember what Eve said when he was born: I have gotten a man from the Lord. John says, “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was Satan’s baby, spiritually. He is the murderer from the beginning in whom the truth did not abide; John is saying what Christ said in John 8:44.

“And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” He abode not in the truth, but Abel was righteous. And Cain killed Abel savagely, not just a cut of the throat. It was very bad.

sense.text: “The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair”. What did Eve say of Cain? I have gotten a man from the Lord. So the daughters of men are Cain’s children, and the sons of God are the line of Adam through Seth (Genesis 5:1-3). The sons of God started messing around with Cain’s daughters: “they took them wives of all which they chose.” The sons of God started to marry into the line of Cain.

“My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh”: man is fallible, man makes mistakes. “Yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years”: the Lord cut man’s life short because the sons of God began to mingle with the daughters of men.

“There were giants in the earth in those days”: in the time the sons of God and the daughters of men got together. “When the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men”, married the daughters of Cain, and they bare children to them, “the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Powerful hybrid babies, pretty much, but extremely wicked.

The renown is the fame and the power; the mighty goes into the wickedness they were doing. That is why Nimrod was called a mighty hunter before the Lord. They were powerful, fierce, renowned fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain.

“The wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” What did Cain build when he was cast out? A city. The sons of God started to dwell in that city, learn of Cain and follow behind his ways. Kind of like today: the sons of God messing around with Esau again, dwelling in his city and learning his ways.

“It repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth”. “I will destroy man”: now the sons of God were behaving like Cain and his daughters. God was so mad he would destroy everything, “both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air”, and start over.

“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God of that time doing wickedness with Cain’s line, Noah did not. There is always a light that shines in the darkness all throughout time; the earth is shrouded in darkness and there is always that light that shimmers.

“Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations”: righteous, keeping God’s commandments, the commandments that Seth kept. “And Noah walked with God”: he walked with God when he was keeping the commandments, like Abraham.

“The earth also was corrupt before God”, because the sons of God learned from and mingled with the daughters of men, Cain’s children. Cain gained dominion on the earth; he was already around and had built his city before Seth was born.

“And the earth was filled with violence”, just as Cain was violent. Is the earth full of violence today? Yes.

“All flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.” “The earth is filled with violence through them”: through the sons of God and the daughters of men. “Behold, I will destroy them with the earth”: everybody.

precepts.why:
“In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him”: God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God.

“Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Adam was made in the image of God, and Seth was made in Adam’s image. Was Cain made in Adam’s image? No.

So the sons of God came out of the line of Adam, through Seth, and the daughters of men came from the line of Cain. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain’s daughters.

Luke counts the line back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” Adam was the son of God, so Seth was of the sons of God. Seth’s line were the sons of God. Abel was one, but Cain killed him, and Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel.

Cain was a man from the Lord, a regular man. God made him, but he was not God’s son: he was somebody else’s son, of that wicked one. Everyone is not made in God’s image. Cain was not made in God’s image; Seth was, and Abel was.
Back to Cain: Eve “bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” So the daughters of men, the daughters of man, are Cain’s children.
To prove what it means that Noah walked with God: the Lord said to Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Walk before me and be perfect means keep his commandments.

How you walk before the Lord: “Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” Walking with God does not mean long walks and talks on the beach. It means they walked in his ways.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments, just as Noah did. Noah was perfect in his generations like Abraham was.

sense.text:
Rebekah conceived, “and the children struggled together within her”. Remember Eve had Cain first, and then Abel.

“If it be so, why am I thus?” If this is the blessing of God, why am I hurting, why am I in this condition? “And she went to enquire of the Lord.”

“Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. They are twins, but two different nations, two different races, not the same. Their manners, how they look, how they think, how they behave, will be completely different. Twins, identical or fraternal, usually think alike or act alike and finish each other’s sentences, but these are two different people.

One will kill a whole race of people and say they killed themselves. You will never come across history where black folks went and eradicated an entire race from the earth, dropped nukes on anybody, or killed animals into extinction. We don’t swim around with sharks or get thrown 80 feet in the air by a bison. Black folks look at the bison at the zoo, behind a cage. Leave God’s creatures alone, Esau: they don’t like you either. Go play with the sharks; both of y’all are great and white.

“And the one people shall be stronger than the other people”: that is us, stronger than them. “And the elder shall serve the younger”: they served us under David. After the fall of both kingdoms, Judah and Israel, we lost dominion over them, and they started to ascend into power again.

“There were twins in her womb.” “And the first came out red”: the first, the eldest, came out red, all over. “And they called his name Esau.” That pigmentation was gone, just as the Lord told Cain in the beginning: cursed from the earth, you are going to look different. The Lord sent him right back looking the exact same way as before.
“His hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob”. That fight continued even after they were born.

“Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field”. What did Cain do? The same exact thing. Nothing new under the sun: no thing, and no one, is new under the sun.

“And Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.” Esau dwelt in the field like Cain, and Abel was a shepherd who brought the firstlings of his flock.

precepts.why: “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Eve bare Cain first and then Abel; Rebekah bare Esau first and then Jacob. Cain was the man of the field and Abel the shepherd; Esau was the man of the field, and Jacob was the shepherd (Genesis 30). The same people doing the same thing again.

sense.text: “Thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above”.

“And by thy sword shalt thou live”. That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around lands that do not belong to him, acquiring by the sword, killing, massacring and destroying everything, and holding himself unaccountable.

We civilized the Native Americans; we didn’t steal the land, we conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, you did not give it back. You kept the land, gave it to your children, and passed laws to give it to other white folks who came afterwards and conquered nothing, the Irish and the British. You gave land that did not belong to you. That is stealing.

“And shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” Once the kings out of David’s loins went off, Esau was able to break free from our rule and start to conquer.

“Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him”. “The days of mourning for my father are at hand”: Isaac is going to be dead soon. “Then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing.

“Thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.” How evil that is: your brother would find comfort for himself by killing you. Killing you would make him comfortable.
“Flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran”, the uncle’s house, “and tarry with him a few days, until thy brother’s fury turn away”, until he calms down, because he wants you dead.
“Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew that if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, you are going to die too. If he kills you, he has to be killed.

precepts.why:
“But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger”. The unrighteous is Cain, the murderer from the beginning who abode not in the truth; he went away from her in his anger.

“He perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” When Cain killed Abel, it was not just a tap on the back of the head. He brutally killed Abel in his fury, and Cain was killed too, murdered in the same violent way he killed Abel. That is why Rebekah said, why should I be deprived of you both in one day. He got killed bad as well.

“Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man; which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: they are liars.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man”. The Bible calls the evil man, the violent man, the wicked. The one who lives by the sword is the violent man.

“I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob”, just like he loved Abel. “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste”: he allowed him to be overthrown.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: we lost it all, going back to being vagabonds, poor. “But we will return and build the desolate places”: build ourselves up as an empire. “They shall build”, like Cain built that city, “but I will throw down”.

“And they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: the beginning and the end of wickedness. “And, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: righteous anger forever. No repentance, no salvation, no kingdom ever, not even the good ones. So some of you coons out there.

Christ names the violent man: “the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven is Israel. The violent are the Romans, and Esau is the Romans. Esau is the violent man, the wicked man: by his sword he lives.

sense.text: Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother’s house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban. “And Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” Jacob dealt with the flocks of Laban.
Jacob set the pilled rods before the flocks in the watering troughs, “and the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ringstraked, speckled, and spotted”: different kinds.
“He put his own flocks by themselves, and put them not unto Laban’s cattle.” Jacob had his own flocks and Laban had his; he did not mingle them together.

“So the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s. And the man increased exceedingly”.

Jacob was Laban’s shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just like Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just like Cain was a man of the field.

precepts.why:
Jacob speaking to Laban: “This twenty years have I been with thee; thy ewes and thy she goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it”.

“In the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” I worked hard for you, Laban, and you are doing me dirty. “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.” Laban was a grimy dude; he did Jacob dirty.

The fact of the matter is that Jacob was the one who handled the flocks. He was a shepherd, and dealt with the flocks the same way Abel dealt with the flocks.

sense.text: Abel was killed, and then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel. Adam “begat a son in his own likeness, after his image”: meaning a son of God.

“He begat sons and daughters”. It keeps saying they begat sons and daughters, but it names specific names, because those children were significant: they birthed prophets, the righteous ones. Among the other sons and daughters, all hell was going on; there was wickedness. If you live that long, you have a whole bunch of children, and of all of them it names this one and that one.

That is why Noah is named as perfect. He had brothers and siblings, but he is mentioned because he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of that time who were dealing with the daughters of men. Noah didn’t deal with that.
“Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch”. Wait a minute: did Cain not have a son named Enoch too? So weird, right?
“And Enoch walked with God”, just like Noah walked with God. “And he was not; for God took him”: he was taken up the way Elijah was.

“Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech”. Didn’t Cain have a Lamech? There are always two, the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth’s line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Left hand side, right hand side: righteous Enoch, evil-ass Enoch.
“All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years”: the longest of any man ever.

“This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed.” When Adam sinned, the Lord cursed the ground, and it was hard for them to cultivate the land. After Noah, they said, he will give us some comfort.

“Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Remember Shem and Seth were had in great honour (Ecclesiasticus 49:16). And remember Noah was five hundred years old when he had them.

precepts.why: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Shem, Noah’s son, and Seth were held in great honour. Adam had his righteous child, Seth, and Noah had his righteous child, Shem, and out of Shem’s line came us. Seth and Shem got that honour, as Adam did.

“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “There are two and two, one against another.”

There is always a good side and a bad side. There was a righteous Enoch and there was a wicked one.

These are Cain’s kids, the men, the daughters of men: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.”

So Cain had a son named Enoch, one named Methusael, and one named Lamech, and Seth’s line had its Enoch, its Methuselah and its Lamech. The wicked side and the righteous side, two and two.

sense.text: “For thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” He saw Noah as righteous by his keeping the commandments. This generation of yours has got to go; I have to kill everybody but you.

“Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens”, and of the beasts that are not clean by two. How would you know which ones are clean and unclean if you had no laws? Noah knew the difference between the clean and the unclean because Noah was keeping the laws, the commandments. That is how he walked with God and was found righteous and perfect.

“To keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth”: to preserve life.
“Every living substance that I have made will I destroy from off the face of the earth.” I am going to destroy everything.
“And Noah did according unto all that the Lord commanded him”: he built the ark.

“Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.” He was five hundred years old when he begat Shem, Ham and Japheth, and six hundred when the flood came: a hundred years later Noah got in that boat. That gives a span of a hundred years in which the ark was being built. So what was Noah doing in that time? Was he just sitting around building a boat, waiting for the rain to come? No.
“Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him, into the ark”.

“All the fountains of the great deep broken up”: an earthquake under the water, and that causes tsunamis, and destroyed everything. “And the windows of heaven were opened”: then the rain on top of that, forty days and forty nights.

So the Lord flooded the whole earth and killed everything, dead and gone, except what was on that boat: eight people. Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives.
“In the selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth”, with Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons, and every beast after his kind, “every bird of every sort.”

“And the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close the door; God did. Why? Because you hear what is outside: let us in! A man has a soft spot and would open the door. God said, nah, I got it. No one can get in, banging and crying. You had a hundred years to figure it out. They were warned; God was longsuffering. I told y’all, repent, stop following Cain, stop following the white man, keep these laws. We good. Okay: hope you’re a good swimmer.

We read this all the time and don’t understand what Noah dealt with. Babies out there, people screaming, please, my baby. His own family was out there too, his siblings. Noah, his sons and their wives had to sit there and hear the screaming, the crying, the begging, until you hear nothing no more. That is a terrible thing to experience.

precepts.why:
Within that hundred-year span, what was Noah doing? “By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain”, as we read earlier, “and by it he being dead yet speaketh”: his righteousness speaks even though he is dead and gone. We know he was a righteous man by his actions. “By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death”: taken up the same way Elijah was.

“By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet”: rain forty days and forty nights, the whole earth flooded, everyone on earth dead. That was unseen, unheard of. The Lord said, Noah, I am going to kill everybody; get the animals, get your wife, your sons and their wives, get in the boat. Noah had no questions; he was faithful like Abraham. In that hundred years he could have said, it ain’t bad here, I don’t believe it’s going to happen. He said no: build, let’s get out of here.

“Moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world”: Noah got saved and everybody else didn’t. “And became heir of the righteousness which is by faith”: Noah kept the commandments of God, and by faith he built that boat. That was his works; his faith was proven by his building the ark. Faith without works is dead.

“For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God”, to his Father. “Being put to death in the flesh”: Christ was a man. It does not say put to death in the God and the flesh. He was not a demigod, half and half, like Hercules; he was a man with spiritual power. “But quickened by the Spirit”: brought back to life by the spirit after three days.

“He went and preached unto the spirits in prison”: in captivity. That is his people, us. “Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah”. Keep that word longsuffering. The Lord gave a hundred-year span for the people to repent: the flood is coming. And what made God longsuffering, what was he doing? 2 Peter 2 shows it.

“And many shall follow their pernicious ways”: false prophets. “Through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you”: lying words.

“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell”. The angels here are the sons of God in Genesis 6, Seth’s line, who messed around with the daughters of men. He destroyed them.

“And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness”. What was Noah? A preacher of righteousness. When it says God was longsuffering, Noah was preaching repentance: y’all better repent; the Most High is going to kill you all. For a hundred years they said, not here, we good, we mighty, we well off, look at my white girl here, look at Becky. They mocked him for building a big old boat for no reason. Between his five hundredth year and his six hundredth year God gave them a span of time to get themselves together, and they did not listen.

Noah was a preacher of righteousness while the sons of God were mingling with the daughters of men. What did Noah do? Tobit tells his son: “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. Take a wife of your own kind; do not marry outside your nation; do not marry a heathen woman.

“For we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred”. They all married wives of their own kindred, including Noah. Noah married a daughter of God, not a daughter of men. His wife was his own kind, and his sons’ wives were their own kind.

Noah did not step outside of that and mess with Cain’s daughters, as the sons of God were doing. He kept the laws of God and married his own. Tobit kept that law, and his sons and their wives kept it too.

Why the Lord shut the door: “he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth”. That is Christ.

Right now repentance is open. This is the longsuffering, the time right now to get it right. Once that door is closed, that’s it; no one can open it.

sense.text: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul”, “and didst breathe into him the breath of life”: as we read earlier in Genesis 2.
“And thou leadest him into paradise”: Adam was in paradise, heaven on earth, with them twelve gates.

“Unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations”: all the way down.

“Of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Adam had nations. They lived a long time, and living that long they had many children that divided into nations; that is how Cain had his wife and Seth got his wife.

There were tribes back then, and what were they called? The sons of God. Sounds like Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. Moses was told to write it down as the sons of God for now, but the Lord knew we would figure it out. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; the righteous, Abel and Seth, were around then and are around now; and the wicked, evil leaders were around back then and are around now.

“And every people walked after their own will”: after Adam died, every people did what they wanted. “And did wonderful things before thee”: wonderful here means evil. They started to mess around with the daughters of men. “And despised thy commandments”: the commandments were around back then. That is how Noah knew the difference between the clean and the unclean. Not Noah: Noah didn’t despise them.
“And again in process of time”, just as it said of Cain, “thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them.” “As death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.”

“Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” Who are the righteous men? That goes back to Shem, Shem’s line: not Ham’s line, not Japheth’s line. That is why Shem and Seth were had in great honour (Ecclesiasticus 49:16).

precepts.why:
Remember Cain wandered off, built a city, a metropolis, and named it after his son Enoch, and acquired power on the earth. “His brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp”. Cain’s line handled music; they were behind all the music back then. Music is very influential, very powerful in the wrong hands, and it is in the wrong hands today. The talent of music may have come from the sons of God, but Cain’s people were behind the evil music, just like today. Nothing new under the sun.

“Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: a master inventor in brass and iron, which means weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Esau was a man of war; that was Esau’s blessing, and it was Cain’s too. Cain built a city, had musical influence and battle influence; he was a conqueror, like he is today.

“Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.” Seth was Abel’s replacement of righteousness.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Seth’s line is the line where God started talking to us again. When the sons of God despised his commandments, God stopped dealing with us; by the time Seth was born, we were in madness. But once Seth and Enos came, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started listening and dealing with us again.

So the wickedness is always around, and the righteous is always born within the evil.

The chapter praises the famous men, our fathers that begat us, renowned for their power and declaring prophecies. “The people will tell of their wisdom, and the congregation will shew forth their praise”: that is the leaders.

“Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.” Enoch was involved in wickedness too, but he was an example of repentance.

“Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world”: the time of wrath, the flood. Damn. “Therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came.” The Lord destroyed all the earth, kept Noah alive, and started all over again with him.

sense.text: What does the flood of Noah represent? “In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment”. Thee is Israel. The Lord’s wrath upon us is our captivity, and even now we are in captivity. “But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee”: he will grant us mercy.

“For this is as the waters of Noah unto me”: our being captive is as the waters of Noah. “For as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth; so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee.”

The Lord flooded the earth and made a vow with the rainbow that he would never flood the earth again. In the same way he will never put us in captivity again once he redeems us. You will not see slavery ever again; we will be ruling forever. This is the last go-around.

“For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed”: destruction, no more nations. “But my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed”: his mercy will not depart from us.

So the Lord saying he would not flood the earth any more, and the rainbow, is symbolic of the Lord having mercy upon his people before Israel even existed: freeing us from captivity and sending his son to die for us. The rainbow goes back to us, the sun goes back to us, the moon goes back to us. Everything on this earth, inside of it and outside of it, refers back to God’s people and God’s mercy toward that people. No one else.

“When the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously”: the context is the land, punishing the people on the land. “And will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it”.

“Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness”. That is what Noah did, and his wife, his sons and their wives: they saved themselves by their own righteousness. Likewise Daniel, likewise Job.

“Or if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my fury upon it in blood”: Noah, Daniel and Job each faced such things. “They shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness.”

Noah saved his own soul and his house, and the people had a long time to figure it out before that door got closed. You deliver yourself only by your own righteousness. That goes for the man, the wife and the children: it is on you. Everyone must work out their own soul’s salvation with fear and trembling.
“This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king.” The dream the Lord showed King Nebuchadnezzar of the empires that would follow behind his in time.
“Thou art this head of gold.” In the great image Nebuchadnezzar saw in his dream, the head of gold is Babylon.
“After thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee”: the Medes joined with the Persians, the silver. “And another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth”: Greece.
“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron”: Rome. Remember what Cain specialized in: brass and iron, weapons and war. The same thing; nothing new under the sun.

“Whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided”: that is America. “But there shall be in it of the strength of the iron”: Rome’s power, military might.

precepts.why:
The head of gold was Babylon, the silver Media and Persia, the brass Greece, the iron Rome, and the feet iron and clay. “And saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns”: this beast is the fourth, the toes. Rather than ten toes, this beast has ten horns: the same exact beast with a different attribute. On the statue it is the toes of the feet; in Daniel 7 it is the fourth beast; in Esdras it is an eagle; in Revelation it is a dragon.

“Like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion”. This empire took all the ancient civilizations before it and merged them into itself. The leopard is the Greek philosophy, the democracy and politics of America; the feet of a bear is Persia; the mouth of a lion is the Babylonian doctrines found in America. It took all the ancient dark civilizations, learned from their mistakes, and merged them into itself.

“And the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” Last but not least, Satan rules over him, as the Lord told Cain, thou shalt rule over him. The same power Cain gained back then through the music and the warfare, he gains here now.

“I saw one of his heads as it were wounded to death; and his deadly wound was healed”: the Renaissance. “And they worshipped the dragon which gave power unto the beast”: they worshipped Satan. “Who is able to make war with him?” Because he acquired power.

“He exerciseth all the power of the first beast”: the iron, the legs. He causes the earth to worship the first beast through the church system.

“He maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men”: nuclear power, nuclear warfare, fire power. “And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles”: miracles is another word for technology, which he had power to do in the sight of the beast, his own people, Germany and Russia.

“That they should make an image to the beast”: an image dedicated to the captive church: the white image of Christ. That is the image of the beast.

“I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.” She is counted as the eighth head. She is “arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls”: wealthy and powerful. “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.”

Why is this important? Judgments are like a ring. The image Nebuchadnezzar saw began with the head of gold, Babylon. The fourth beast goes into the toes of the image, then into the unnamed fourth beast of Daniel 7, the eagle of Ezra, the dragon of Revelation. So Babylon was first, and it ends with Babylon again: America. Full circle, just as a ring. Babylon reigned over us, and now Babylon reigns over us again. It is a whole loop. Nothing new under the sun.

sense.text: “I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance: that ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets”.

“There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts”, like in Noah’s time. They did not believe Noah, building the boat for no reason. Noah’s crazy, look at him over there, his crazy sons and wives building a boat for no reason. They were scoffing.

“Where is the promise of his coming?” Where is your rain at? Where is this judgment coming from? “All things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation”: this is how the world is supposed to be; this ain’t captivity, we free.
“By the word of God the heavens were of old”: the heavens of old are Cain’s kingdom, the ruling class of old, “and the earth standing out of the water and in the water”, which ended up being flooded.
“Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished”: they all died.

“But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.” By the same word: the word Noah preached to the people before the flood. The same word was preached by Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech and Noah to the wicked of our people mingled among the other people of that time, and the flood came and killed them. Here we are again, preaching the same word to the same wicked sons of God mixed with the same people, before the fire. It is the exact same thing.

“One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”: some men scoff and do not believe the fire is coming.

“But is longsuffering to us-ward”. Remember that word, longsuffering: Noah preached to the people, and God gave time to get it right. “Not willing that any should perish”, drowned to death or burned alive, “but that all should come to repentance”, as Noah was preaching before they were drowned.

“The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, just as the flood came. “The heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.”

“What manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”: like Noah was, and his three sons and his wife and their wives. “The heavens being on fire shall be dissolved”: on fire, as opposed to being under water.
“We, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness”: like in Noah’s time, a new heavens and a new earth.
“Be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.”

precepts.why:
“This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.” The same generation that was around in Christ’s time is here now; they will not pass till all these things he speaks of in the future are fulfilled. “Heaven and earth shall pass away”: with nuclear fire. “But my words shall not pass away”, because they have been preached since Seth, all the way down.

“But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” So it shall be in this time: the exact same people who were ruling in Noah’s time will be ruling in this time. The same ignorance Noah faced back then, we face now, and the same word he preached back then, we preach now. Nothing new under the sun.

“They were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark”: eating, drinking, sleeping around, until Noah got in that boat. “And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away”: they did not see it coming, and they were all put to death.

Why did the flood come? Who caused the flood, and who causes the fire? Remember the beast in Revelation has fire come down from heaven: he is behind that.

“When the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain, and he got killed the same way he killed his brother. “For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood”: Cain’s cause. Whose evil was responsible for the earth being flooded? Cain’s evil, and the sons of God dealt with them. If you are all for Cain now, I will kill all of you.

Likewise today: the Lord promised with the rainbow that he would not flood the earth again, the same way he promised mercy to his people. He will not flood it a second time, but he will burn it.

“Come out of her, my people”: come out of Babylon. “That ye be not partakers of her sins”. Whose sins do we not partake in? Edom’s sins, the same way the sons of God should not have partaken in the sins of the daughters of men back then, that Noah was preaching against. It is the exact same thing all over again.

“And that ye receive not of her plagues.” Her plague back then was water; her plague now is going to be fire.

“For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.” As the Lord remembered Cain’s: these are evil, and I have to destroy them.
